detail.title: Collateral Algorithmic Enforcement: When Language Is Not Understanding-Platform Governance Failures and the Rise of Large Understanding Models
detail.abstract:
Platform governance is increasingly executed through automated systems operating under conditions of scale, uncertainty, and regulatory pressure. While these systems aim to detect harmful content and behavior, they frequently produce unintended consequences, including false-positive enforcement actions affecting legitimate users and businesses. This paper conceptualizes these outcomes as Collateral Algorithmic Enforcement (CAE)—systematic externalities arising from language-centric AI architectures applied to understanding-centric governance problems.

Drawing on recent advances in AI research and platform governance literature, the paper argues that Large Language Models (LLMs), while effective in pattern recognition and text generation, remain structurally limited in contextual reasoning, intent inference, and causal attribution. These limitations become particularly salient in high-impact enforcement decisions, where misclassification can lead to economic and reputational harm.

Building on prior work introducing Large Understanding Models (LUMs), this paper proposes a paradigm shift toward AI systems that integrate semantic comprehension, contextual modeling, causal reasoning, and explainable decision-making. A Platform Governance Risk Framework (PGRF) is developed to model the propagation of enforcement decisions into downstream business impacts.

The paper outlines a multi-layered empirical research design and identifies key hypotheses regarding enforcement risk, automation intensity, and economic externalities. The findings contribute to the literature on AI governance, platform economics, and algorithmic accountability by reframing moderation failures as a consequence of architectural limitations rather than operational deficiencies

title: Zero-Beta Decorrelation in Structural Liquidity Strategies: Theoretical Implications of a Decade-Spanning Empirical Anomaly

detail.title: Zero-Beta Decorrelation in Structural Liquidity Strategies: Theoretical Implications of a Decade-Spanning Empirical Anomaly
detail.abstract: A companion study to Boutgajouft (2026a), this paper examines the theoretical implications of a systematic trading strategy exhibiting near-zero market beta (β m ≈ 0, statistically indistinguishable from zero across all regimes tested over 2008-2025) with positive returns attributable to a structural liquidity factor F SL rather than to conventional market exposure. Rather than presenting backtesting data-which is documented in the companion report-this paper investigates why this property is anomalous within the existing financial economics literature and what it implies for portfolio theory, factor models, and the taxonomy of alternative investments. We introduce a formal four-category taxonomy of decorrelation mechanisms, distinguishing between apparent, conditional, mechanical, and structural decorrelation. We argue that the BLT Engine represents the first documented instance of Category IV (structural) decorrelation-where near-zero beta arises from the instrument universe construction and return-generating mechanism rather than from statistical averaging, active hedging, or offsetting exposures. Through spanning analysis, we demonstrate that such a return stream is non-replicable by any linear combination of market-correlated assets. We examine the implications for the Capital Asset Pricing Model, the Efficient Market Hypothesis, and multi-factor frameworks, arguing that the observed return profile implies either a missing risk factor or a capacity-constrained structural inefficiency. Finally, we discuss the portfolio construction value of structurally decorrelated strategies and their optimal allocation within institutional frameworks.

title: De-Lock-In: Veto Network Neutralization and the End of Military-Technological Lock-In

detail.title: De-Lock-In: Veto Network Neutralization and the End of Military-Technological Lock-In
detail.abstract: Path dependence theory explains why incumbent technologies persist. It does not explain how persistence ends. This paper proposes a termination mechanism for technological lock-in in weapon systems under concentrated state procurement: veto network neutralization. Incumbent weapon systems generate stakeholder networks that possess institutional control over procurement, doctrine, and career advancement. Technical superiority of alternatives is insufficient to overcome this veto capacity. Transition occurs when incumbent stakeholders lose formal control at institutional veto nodes-and when sufficient replacement capacity exists to absorb the shift. The paper demonstrates this mechanism through four cases: the English longbow-to-firearm transition (1340-1595), the battleship-to-aircraft carrier transition (1918-1942), the sail-to-steam naval transition (1815-1860), and the heavy cavalry-to-infantry firearms transition in early modern Europe. Each case exhibits a characteristic temporal signature: a long lag between technical feasibility and adoption while veto networks remain intact, followed by rapid adoption once veto capacity is neutralized, with post-neutralization tempo mediated by replacement capacity. The mechanism is conditional, operating only in paradigmatic transitions under concentrated procurement authority, and falsifiable, generating testable predictions about timing, tempo, and comparative variation.

title: Gender Differences in Pension Investment: The Role of Biased Advice
affiliations: Free University of Bolzano-Bozen, Faculty of Economics and Management, , University of Trento and Free University of Bozen-Bolzano

detail.title: Gender Differences in Pension Investment: The Role of Biased Advice
detail.abstract: We study whether gender-biased financial advice contributes to the gender gap in pension wealth. Using administrative records from four private pension funds in Italy, we document that women are ceteris paribus 8 percentage points less likely than men to choose stock-focused investment lines at the time of enrollment. To assess whether advisory behavior contributes to this gap, we conduct a vignette-based survey experiment among pension advisors affiliated to the four funds, randomly varying the gender of otherwise identical prospective 25-year-old clients. Advisors are 22 percentage points less likely to recommend stock-oriented portfolios to female clients, even after conditioning on advisors' beliefs about relevant client characteristics. We further show that a simple information intervention that makes advisors aware of the documented gender bias eliminates this gap in the experimental setting. Linking advisors to real clients in the administrative data, we demonstrate that the gender gap in actual investment choices shrinks by approximately 60% during the five months following the intervention. This evidence suggests that gender bias in financial advice is largely implicit and that low-cost informational feedback to advisors can meaningfully reduce gender disparities in retirement wealth accumulation.

title: Beyond Truth: From Epistemic Situatedness to Scientific Ethics as Method

detail.title: Beyond Truth: From Epistemic Situatedness to Scientific Ethics as Method

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This paper examines a philosophical inquiry into the nature of understanding, reasoning, and scientific progress, beginning with a fundamental question: Is judgement possible without context, perspective, or presupposition? A negative answer prompts a reconsideration of "absolute truth" and "causality" within scientific practice. After surveying positions ranging from scientific realism to instrumentalism, the paper argues that scientific progress is better conceived as a collective departure from recognised error rather than an approach towards an unattainable absolute truth. The discussion does not remain epistemically neutral. By adopting a sober, historically informed view of scientific motivation and the power structures within which science operates, the paper contends that the preservation of reliable public science requires the institutional adoption of scientific ethics as method-not as an individual virtue, but as a structural condition for the continued viability of science. The aim is not to offer a comprehensive ethical theory, but to articulate a conceptual framework demonstrating its necessity.

title: Paid Caregiving Leave Policies and an Update on Paid Parental Leave
affiliations: George Mason University, Stanford University and Stanford University

detail.title: Paid Caregiving Leave Policies and an Update on Paid Parental Leave
detail.abstract: Paid leave policies are designed to help workers balance work with caregiving responsibilities, yet research has focused predominantly on parental leave while the literature on non-parental caregiving leave remains nascent. This chapter reviews the evidence on the impacts of paid family leave (PFL) and paid sick leave (PSL) policies, with a focus on non-childbirth-related caregiving. We begin with an overview of the prevalence and challenges of informal caregiving in the US and internationally, followed by a description of the current paid caregiving leave policy landscape. We then review evidence on the impact of these policies on leave take-up, labor market outcomes, caregiver health and well-being, employer outcomes, and utilization of formal care. We find that paid leave policies have successfully increased leave take-up and that PFL improves labor market outcomes for workers with caregiving responsibilities, without adversely affecting employers. There is also some suggestive evidence of improvements in caregivers’ mental health. We additionally provide an update of the paid parental leave literature since it was last reviewed by Rossin-Slater (2018), describing the latest evidence on maternal health, child health and development, parental labor market outcomes, and employer outcomes. We conclude by identifying key gaps in the literature, including the lack of research on the outcomes of (non-child) care recipients, limited evidence on employer responses, and the underexplored role of PSL in supporting caregiving needs.

title: The Generalized Productivity Equation: A Cross-Scale Structural Theory of R×N×A From Micro Individuals to Macro Entities
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Generalized Productivity Equation: A Cross-Scale Structural Theory of R×N×A From Micro Individuals to Macro Entities
detail.abstract: Two dominant traditions have shaped our understanding of individual effectiveness and human flourishing: the principle-centered paradigm of personal development (Covey, 1989) and the positive psychology movement, including Seligman's (2002, 2011) well-being theory (PERMA), Deci and Ryan's (2000) Self-Determination Theory (SDT), and Csikszentmihalyi's (1990) flow theory. Despite their considerable achievements, both traditions share a common structural limitation: they describe what effectiveness or well-being looks like, or prescribe what to do, but neither provides a unified generative mechanism explaining how these outcomes are structurally produced—or why they systematically fail to materialize for individuals who faithfully follow prescribed principles. Two persistent anomalies illustrate this gap: (1) highly disciplined individuals frequently hit structural growth ceilings despite faithful adherence to prescribed habits, and (2) previously successful individuals rapidly decline when macro-environments undergo paradigm shifts—even while maintaining their established routines. To address these theoretical gaps, this paper performs an isomorphic mapping of core concepts from Marxian political economy—means of production, relations of production, and productive forces—onto the micro-level of individual life trajectories. We propose the R×N×A framework, a multiplicative equation comprising three structural variables: Resources (R), representing the individual's tangible and intangible asset portfolio; Network (N), representing the individual's relational network structure, platform embeddedness, and trust infrastructure; and Adaptability/Action (A), representing the capacity to sense environmental shifts and dynamically reconfigure R and N. Ten theoretical propositions are developed across four domains. First, propositions 1–5 demonstrate that Covey's seven habits are not independent success factors but rather specific mechanisms for building R (Habits 1–3), constructing N (Habits 4–6), and activating A (Habit 7). Second, proposition 6 explores the scale-free isomorphism of R×N×A across individual, organizational, and macro-entity levels. Third, proposition 7 introduces a three-layer architecture of personal development theories—outcome layer (Seligman's PERMA), principle layer (Covey's Habits), and generative layer (R×N×A)—arguing that positive psychology's well-being constructs are experiential outputs of R×N×A structural configurations rather than independently pursuable inputs, and that Self-Determination Theory's three basic needs (Competence, Relatedness, Autonomy) map structurally onto R, N, and A respectively. Fourth, propositions 8–10 extend the framework to cross-domain frontiers: AI-driven structural redistribution of value weights within the R×N×A equation (proposition 8), the integration with the Theory of Purposeful Work Behavior (Barrick, Mount, & Li, 2013) to explain when purposeful goal strivings produce collaborative synergy versus friction (proposition 9), and a structural reinterpretation of the "law of attraction" (proposition 10).

title: Dynamic Adjustment to Trade Shocks
affiliations: University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - University of California, San Diego, World Bank Group, University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - Department of Economics and University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Dynamic Adjustment to Trade Shocks

keywords: estimation of the elasticity of trade

detail.abstract: Global trade flows and supply chains adjust gradually. Empirical estimates of the trade elasticity for the short run are a fraction of those for the long run and suggest that trade is subject to substantive dynamic frictions. We develop a tractable framework that provides microfoundations for trade adjustment and rationalizes estimation of a time-varying trade elasticity. The model features forward-looking firms facing sticky sourcing choices and nests a version of the Eaton-Kortum model as a limiting long-run case. We calibrate the model and quantify the impacts of two events: the 2004 EU Eastern enlargement (an anticipated change) and the 2018 US-China trade war (an arguably unanticipated change). Our findings suggest that sourcing frictions and anticipation effects alter the time pattern of specialization, can result in short-term welfare losses but long-term gains, and can drive marked trade adjustments before anticipated shocks occur.

title: Comparative Assessment of Climate-Responsive Design and Occupant Behaviour Across Türkiye's Building Typologies for Enhanced Utilisation and Performance

detail.title: Comparative Assessment of Climate-Responsive Design and Occupant Behaviour Across Türkiye's Building Typologies for Enhanced Utilisation and Performance
detail.abstract: This study evaluates and compares the sustainability performance of selected historic, commercial, and institutional buildings in Istanbul to identify effective climate-responsive and energy-efficient design strategies. The objectives are to assess performance using LEEDbased criteria, examine variations across building typologies, and outline implications for future sustainable design. Using an evaluation matrix, responses from 175 experts were analysed across key LEED categories for seven case study buildings. The comparative assessment reveals notable variations in sustainability performance across the seven evaluated buildings. ERKE Green Academy consistently achieved the highest mean scores (≈4.40-4.60), particularly in Sustainable Sites, Water Efficiency, Energy and Atmosphere, and Indoor Environmental Quality. This strong performance reflects its integration of advanced green technologies, optimised daylighting strategies, biophilic elements, and smart system controls. Modern commercial towers, such as the Allianz Tower and Sapphire Tower, recorded strong mean scores (≈4.20-4.50) across categories related to Integrative Design, Energy Efficiency, and Materials and Resources. Their performance is largely driven by intelligent façade systems, double-skin envelopes, automated shading, and highperformance mechanical systems that enhance operational efficiency. In contrast, heritage buildings including Hagia Sophia and Sultan Ahmed Mosque demonstrated moderate yet stable performance levels (≈4.00-4.40). Their strengths were most evident in Indoor Environmental Quality, where passive systems such as thermal mass, natural ventilation, and inherent spatial configurations contribute significantly to occupant comfort. Overall, the findings underscore the complementary value of combining traditional passive strategies with modern smart technologies to achieve resilient, low-energy, and user-responsive architecture. This study is novel as it uniquely demonstrates how traditional passive design strategies and modern smart technologies can be integrated to enhance climate-responsive and energy-efficient performance across diverse building typologies. The study recommends enhanced indoor air quality strategies, occupant education on system use, and stronger policy alignment with LEED standards.

detail.abstract: This paper examines institutional blindness toward cognitive outliers across governance, organizational, scientific, and educational systems. Cognitive outliers are defined as individuals whose cognitive profiles, reasoning patterns, or problem-solving capacities fall outside dominant institutional expectations and standardized processing frameworks. While such outliers frequently generate innovation, strategic insight, or scientific advancement, institutional systems often fail to recognize, integrate, or retain them. The paper analyzes structural and procedural mechanisms that contribute to institutional blindness and explores the systemic consequences of excluding cognitive outliers. By framing institutional blindness as a design limitation rather than a failure of recognition, the study offers a transferable analytical model applicable to leadership selection, innovation governance, and knowledge-intensive environments.

title: The Mena Dominance Law: Viability-Governed Control Under Experimental Battery Runs, Risk Tool Evidence, and Simulation Validation

detail.abstract:
This paper evaluates the Mena Dominance Law kernel in applied settings, using the time tracked margin
ΔX(t) = PX(t) − LX(t),
where PX(t) is recoverable potential and LX(t) is imposed load. We test whether viability governed control—policies that actively avoid sustained dominance deficit under fixed boundary rules—changes usable work, deficit exposure, and boundary-adjacent recovery outcomes. First, we report paired battery-discharge experiments on commercial Li-ion packs (four physical packs; one model has two units; NM = NR = 57), comparing constant-current baselines against a viability-governed four-step current schedule near a fixed cutoff. Under identical cutoff rules, the governed policy increases delivered energy and charge to cutoff (median +5.82% Wh; +4.80% Ah), extends runtime (median +63.38%), and reduces initial voltage sag (median
−4.13%). Standardized post-cutoff recovery voltages shift lower under the governed policy; we interpret this as a boundary-adjacent recovery signature under fixed termination logic, not as a degradation claim. Second, we examine StARS as a sociotechnical risk instrument for routing corrective action between agent-channel stress and structure-channel fragility. Third, using CAISO OASIS time series, we simulate single-layer and dual-layer grid governors, which in this simulation reduce deficit exposure versus baseline and show a clear tradeoff between curtailment and residual deficit time/area under reserve headroom admissibility gating. Taken together, the results show that under fixed boundary definitions, dominance-aware control yields measurable policy-conditional differences. The battery experiments provide the primary executed physical evidence in this paper; the StARS and CAISO sections provide secondary operational and simulation validation.

title: Governing Flood Risk in West African Cities: A Comparative Analysis of Institutional Frameworks in Lagos, Accra, and Dakar Against Sendai Framework Priority 2 Benchmarks

detail.title: Governing Flood Risk in West African Cities: A Comparative Analysis of Institutional Frameworks in Lagos, Accra, and Dakar Against Sendai Framework Priority 2 Benchmarks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: West Africa floods repeatedly and devastatingly. Between 2000 and 2024, the sub-region recorded thousands of flood events annually, with an estimated 500,000 people affected by flooding in West Africa alone each year (Dossa et al., 2025). Yet the three largest cities in West Africa, Lagos in Nigeria, Accra in Ghana, and Dakar in Senegal, have each constructed formal institutional architectures for disaster risk governance that are, on paper, aligned with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 (UNDRR, 2015). The persistence of catastrophic flooding in all three cities despite this institutional investment raises a comparative governance question: what does a cross-city analysis reveal about the structural patterns of governance failure in West African urban flood management, and what does that pattern suggest about the gap between Sendai aspirations and operational reality? This paper examines flood risk governance in Lagos, Accra, and Dakar through the five dimensions of Sendai Framework Priority 2: legal and institutional coherence, multilevel governance and decentralization, stakeholder inclusion, transparency and accountability, and policy integration. The comparison reveals a consistent regional pattern in which governance authority is concentrated at levels too remote from where flood risk is actually created and managed, enforcement mechanisms at the local government level are legally underdeveloped, and the integration of flood risk governance into routine planning and land use decisions is either absent or systematically unenforced.

title: Using Large Language Models to Find Variation in Policy Text for Causal Identification

detail.title: Using Large Language Models to Find Variation in Policy Text for Causal Identification
detail.abstract: We develop a pipeline that uses large language models to find quasi-experimental variation in policy text. The pipeline reads policy documents and classifies whether they contain features suitable for regression discontinuity or difference-indifferences designs. The central question is whether a general-purpose LLM can reliably identify quasi-experimental variation in policy text-without access to outcome data or prior literature. On a post-2016 literature benchmark of 125 paper-policy pairs, the pipeline achieves 97.3% DID recall and 88.2% RD recall under a three-run majority vote. To address concerns about training-data contamination, a fresh-bill expert evaluation is in progress. Because the pipeline operates before outcome data are examined, it supports pre-registration of identified designs.

title: Existence: The Splendour of A-Normativity

detail.title: Existence: The Splendour of A-Normativity

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This account portrays existence not as the product of a preordained plan, but as the outcome of a tiny 'deviation' at the universe's dawn. That deviation generates random 'variation' in biological evolution. We are the result of an endless chain of layered random events at every scale of being, unfolds within simple yet powerful laws. The paper examines four layers of chance: cosmic symmetry breaking, random genetic mutations, stochastic gene expression in development, and experience-based synaptic pruning in the brain . This view helps us recognize that our brains and minds are chaotic, fallible, and astonishing systems, grounding authentic self-knowledge in 'certainty in uncertainty' and 'conviction in doubt'.

title: Background to Self-determination: International and Local.

detail.title: Background to Self-determination: International and Local.

publicationDetails.detailsText: This chapter was originally published in The Ethiopian Federation: Formation, Features, and Challenges, (2018), pages 13-45. Pagination in this edition refers to the present volume

detail.abstract: This chapter explores the historical and legal foundations that shaped the Ethiopian federation, emphasising both international and domestic influences on the principle of self-determination. Internationally, the chapter traces the evolution of self-determination through key global events, such as World Wars, UN Charters, and African and European human rights declarations, culminating in a legal and moral framework that justified national liberation. Domestically, it examines the formation of modern Ethiopia through conquest, settler colonialism, and ethnic subjugation, which triggered armed resistance and political movements, particularly by the Oromo and Tigray groups. The chapter also critiques the centralist imperial model and argues that Ethiopia's ethnonational diversity and historical injustices necessitated a federal arrangement as a political solution to longstanding national questions.

title: Conceptual Challenges of Describing Ethiopian Federalism

detail.title: Conceptual Challenges of Describing Ethiopian Federalism
detail.abstract: Scholars keep trying to fit Ethiopia’s federation into familiar labels—ethnic, multinational, socialist, confederal—but none hold up under scrutiny. This chapter explains why. It shows that the confusion comes from two sources: forcing Ethiopia into the existing federal theory, and mixing the history that produced the federation with the constitutional design that emerged from it. The chapter reviews competing descriptors, unpacks ideological and etymological pitfalls, and tests alternatives such as multi-ethnic, multi-national, three-circle, socialist, and “new federal model” federalism. The conclusion is clear: Ethiopia’s design is best understood as national diversity recognition federalism—a constitutional order that treats nations, nationalities, and peoples as sovereign political subjects and guarantees their equality and right to self-determination, including secession.

title: Revisiting a Post Keynesian Explanation of US Inflation

detail.title: Revisiting a Post Keynesian Explanation of US Inflation

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Risk and Financial Management, volume 19, issue 3, 2026[10.3390/jrfm19030202]

detail.abstract: This paper presents an econometric analysis of inflation from a Post Keynesian perspective using quarterly data from 2002 to 2024 for the United States, including the most recent period of inflation after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. I evaluate the continued relevance of the comprehensive Post Keynesian model of inflation using a reduced form equation that incorporates both the aggregate demand-augmented wage-cost markup equation and the wage growth equation which is robust in explaining inflation. The robustness of the model is tested by incorporating different measures of labor market slack, wages, and inflation. The paper finds that the comprehensive model is not robust for the period 2002 to 2024 even when alternative measures for wages, unemployment, and inflation are utilized. This discrepancy arises because the negative relationship between unit labor costs and inflation, observed in the updated model, proved non-robust upon the inclusion of control variables for energy costs and imports. After employing the Prais-Winsten estimation to account for persistent serial correlation, the revised model aligned with the sign conventions of the original Atesoglu wage-cost markup equation. Specifically, while the coefficient for unit labor costs turned positive, it failed to reach statistical significance. Finally, I discuss potential factors for the decrease in the magnitude and significance of the coefficients in the aggregate demand-augmented wage-cost markup model for the period 2002 to 2024 as well as the pass through of wage growth to broader inflation measures.

title: The Transitional Period of Ethiopia, 1991-1995.

detail.title: The Transitional Period of Ethiopia, 1991-1995.

publicationDetails.detailsText: This chapter was originally published in The Ethiopian Federation: Formation, Features, and Challenges, (2018), pages 46-108. Pagination in this edition refers to the present volume

detail.abstract: This chapter analyses Ethiopia’s political transition from 1991 to 1995, a period marked by the collapse of the socialist Derg regime, the rise of ethnonational liberation fronts, and the institutionalisation of multinational federalism. The study reconstructs key diplomatic and military events surrounding the fall of Addis Ababa, including the U.S.-brokered London talks, the coordinated advance of the TPLF/EPRDF and EPLF, and the marginalisation of competing actors such as the OLF. It further examines the Transitional Charter and the Council of Representatives as foundational mechanisms for redesigning state power, codifying national self-determination, and restructuring executive authority. The analysis highlights the strategic calculus of external actors, especially the United States, whose involvement shaped both regime exit and post-conflict governance trajectories. The chapter demonstrates that the transitional period did not constitute a liberal democratic opening; rather, it functioned as a controlled political reset in which the victorious EPRDF consolidated dominance while institutionalising ethnofederal arrangements that defined the subsequent federal order. The findings contribute to broader debates on post-conflict state formation, negotiated transitions, and federalism in divided societies.

title: The Critical Role of Project Management in the Success of Mega Construction Projects: A Conceptual and Analytical Review

detail.title: The Critical Role of Project Management in the Success of Mega Construction Projects: A Conceptual and Analytical Review
detail.abstract: Mega construction projects represent some of the most complex human endeavors due to their massive budgets, extended timelines, and involvement of multiple stakeholders. Despite technological advancements, many large-scale construction projects still suffer from delays, cost overruns, and coordination failures. This paper investigates the critical importance of project management in improving the success rate of mega construction projects. Through a conceptual and analytical review of project management theories, infrastructure case studies, and modern planning practices, the study demonstrates that effective planning, stakeholder management, risk management, and digital project control systems significantly enhance project performance. The findings suggest that project management is not merely a supporting administrative function but rather the primary determinant of project success in large construction developments.

title: A Brave New World of Hiring: A Natural Field Experiment on How Asynchronous Interviews and AI Assessment Reshape Recruitment
affiliations: Monash University, Monash University, Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer and University of Gothenburg

detail.title: A Brave New World of Hiring: A Natural Field Experiment on How Asynchronous Interviews and AI Assessment Reshape Recruitment
detail.abstract: Recent technological advancements are reshaping pathways to employment by automating the interview process. Asynchronous interviews, in which job applicants submit answers to interview questions via an online platform without interacting with an interviewer, are replacing more traditional face-to-face job interviews. At the same time, AI algorithms are now widely used to assess these interview answers. In this paper, we use a field experiment to comprehensively study how these new technologies affect applicants and employers in the recruitment process. Over 3,000 job applicants are randomized into asynchronous audio or video interviews, live online interviews, and a control group. Their job interviews are then assessed by both professional recruiters and a commercial AI recruitment tool used by most Fortune 100 companies. We find that asynchronous interviews cause an over 50% decrease in application continuation, including among the most qualified applicants, and that this decline is largest for women. A complementary vignette experiment provides evidence that this deterrence is driven by perceptions about the competitiveness and fairness of the recruitment process. In terms of assessments, we find that the AI evaluation tool scores women and underrepresented racial minorities higher than human evaluators, while the opposite is true for men, Whites and Asians. We track our applicants' subsequent labor market outcomes and find that the AI assessment tool predicts subsequent employment success substantially better than human recruiters, suggesting that AI captures soft skills and potential that humans overlook. In addition, we provide evidence that, unlike AI, human recruiters' assessments suffer from multiple cognitive biases. Our findings provide some of the first key evidence on how recent technological advances are transforming the hiring process.

title: Spinning Jennies and Silicon: The Economics of Innovating or Evaporating – Creative Destruction and Public Policies
affiliations: Organization for Economic Co-Operation and Development (OECD)

detail.title: Spinning Jennies and Silicon: The Economics of Innovating or Evaporating – Creative Destruction and Public Policies
detail.abstract: This paper reviews the contributions of the 2025 Nobel Prize in Economics laureates, Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt, to our understanding of innovation-driven economic growth, situating their work within the broader evolution of modern growth theory and empirical evidence. It highlights why the Industrial Revolution marked a transition to sustained, self-reinforcing technological progress and shows how Mokyr's emphasis on knowledge, culture and institutions complements Aghion and Howitt's Schumpeterian framework, which formalises innovation as a competitive process of firm entry, exit and technological replacement. The paper then uses these frameworks to interpret the widespread productivity slowdown observed in advanced OECD economies since the mid-2000s, arguing that weakened creative destruction, slower diffusion of frontier technologies, declining business dynamism and policy headwinds are key explanatory factors.

title: Estimating Passenger Benefits from Airline Service Quality: Nonstop vs. Connecting Flight Frequencies
affiliations: University of California, Irvine - Department of Economics and Universitat Rovira i Virgili (URV)

detail.title: Estimating Passenger Benefits from Airline Service Quality: Nonstop vs. Connecting Flight Frequencies
detail.abstract: This paper estimates passenger benefits from airline flight frequencies, recognizing that this task is less straightforward for connecting trips than for nonstop travel. In doing so, the paper joins Yuan and Jia (2026) as the only other study in the literature that confronts the problem of creating a flight-frequency measure for connecting trips. With airlines providing a crucial service in modern economies, the ability to measure the quality of that service is essential, not just for the nonstop service that links larger cities but for the connecting trips involving smaller endpoints that many passengers rely on.
